\sphinxstylestrong{N}on\sphinxstylestrong{L}inear \sphinxstylestrong{P}arametric \sphinxstylestrong{Opt}imization \sphinxstylestrong{Net}work (NLPOpt\sphinxhyphen{}Net) is a GPU supported python package for learning parameters to solution mappings for nonlinear parametric optimization problem.

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\capstart

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.750\linewidth]{{framework}.jpg}
\caption{Figure 1: Overview of the NLPOpt\sphinxhyphen{}Net framework.}\label{\detokenize{index:id1}}\end{figure}


\chapter{Installation}
\label{\detokenize{index:installation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently, NLPOpt\sphinxhyphen{}Net requires Python 3.9 or later and supports installation for both CPU\sphinxhyphen{}only and GPU\sphinxhyphen{}accelerated environments.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
CPU\sphinxhyphen{}only (Linux/macOS/Windows)

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }nlpoptnet
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
GPU (NVIDIA, CUDA 12)

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}nlpoptnet[cuda12]\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\chapter{Quick Overview}
\label{\detokenize{index:quick-overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To give a quick understanding of what we are doing, we are trying to predict a solution (\(y\)) of the parameterized optimization problem,
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
\quad
\min \quad & f(x,y) \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & h(x,y) = 0, \\
& g(x,y) \le 0, \\
& l(x) \le y \le u(x),
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
for a given set of parameter (\(x\)). The core idea is to train a machine learning model in an unsupervised way and predict new solutions. For feasibility guarantee a projection layer is employed. Particularly, we approximate the original problem into a specific structure of quadratic program and solve that to retain feasibility. Graphically, the projection as training progresses would look like this:

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\capstart

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics[width=1.000\linewidth]{{graphical_interpretation}.jpg}
\caption{Figure 2: Graphical interpretation of the projection.}\label{\detokenize{index:id2}}\end{figure}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a detailed idea, we refer readers to \sphinxhref{https://paperlink.com}{this article}. Complete user documentation can be found \sphinxhref{https://putyourdocumentationlink.com}{here}.


\section{Core API}
\label{\detokenize{index:core-api}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NLPOptNet(config=..., type=...)}} is the user\sphinxhyphen{}facing entry point.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.extract(problem.npz)}} loads structured matrices and exposes them as
model attributes like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.Q}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.A}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.b}}, and so on.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.dataset(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.simplex(...)}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.box(...)}} define the
parameter region.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.constraints.box.add(...)}} is separate from general inequalities so the
bound constraints stay on the dedicated projection path.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.optimize()}} trains and returns a result dictionary with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{output\_dir}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{metadata\_path}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summary}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{history}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.load(metadata\_path)}} restores a trained model, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.predict(x\_value)}} returns projected variable predictions.

\end{itemize}


\chapter{General Workflow}
\label{\detokenize{index:general-workflow}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The core ideas can be generalized in a workflow for training and inference tasks.


\section{Model Creation and Training}
\label{\detokenize{index:model-creation-and-training}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Following is a general pseudocode for building and running a problem with NLPOpt\sphinxhyphen{}Net.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nlpoptnet}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{NLPOptNet}

\PYG{n}{CONFIG} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{n}{model} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{NLPOptNet}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{config}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{CONFIG}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{name}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{problem\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{x} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}parameter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{y} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}variable}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{extract}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{path/to/problem\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{objective}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{equality}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{inequality}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{dataset}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{parameters}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{path/to/parameters.csv}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{build}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{optimize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{run\PYGZus{}dir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{output\PYGZus{}dir}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\section{Load and Use a Trained Model}
\label{\detokenize{index:load-and-use-a-trained-model}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
After training, a saved model can be reloaded to inspect the run summary, visualize the training history, and make new predictions.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{reloaded} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{NLPOptNet}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{metadata\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{reloaded}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{summary}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{reloaded}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{plot\PYGZus{}history}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}pred} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{reloaded}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{predict}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{projection\PYGZus{}backend}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{backend/type/for/prediction}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\chapter{Reporting a Bug or Error}
\label{\detokenize{index:reporting-a-bug-or-error}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
We understand that running into issues can be frustrating. If you experience any errors while using NLPOpt\sphinxhyphen{}Net, please let us know so we can address them in future updates.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When reporting a bug, it is helpful to include:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A brief description of the issue

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Relevant code snippets

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Error messages or logs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Steps to reproduce the problem

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Your feedback is greatly appreciated and helps us improve the package.

NLPOpt\sphinxhyphen{}Net takes a dictionary input for configurations. Following is an example of defining the configuration options and creating a model object.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nlpoptnet}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{NLPOptNet}

\PYG{n}{CONFIG} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{epochs}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1000}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{batch\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{40}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{learning\PYGZus{}rate}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1e\PYGZhy{}3}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{train\PYGZus{}frac}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{hidden\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{64}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{hidden\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{seed}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{alpha\PYGZus{}consistency}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{cp\PYGZus{}mode}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{fixed}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{cp\PYGZus{}iters}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{300}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{cp\PYGZus{}tol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1e\PYGZhy{}09}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{safety}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.95}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{knorm\PYGZus{}iters}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{15}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{knorm\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{adjoint\PYGZus{}iters}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{k\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{use\PYGZus{}ruiz}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ruiz\PYGZus{}iters}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{dtype}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{float64}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{print\PYGZus{}every}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{device}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{auto}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{verbose}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{n}{model} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{NLPOptNet}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{config}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{CONFIG}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{qp}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{name}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Example\PYGZus{}QP\PYGZus{}Model}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here, the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CONFIG}} dictionary defines the configuration of the model.
Users must provide all required configuration options. For optional
parameters, if not specified, default values will be used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{type}} argument is used for reference and bookkeeping purposes
only and does not affect any computational procedure. Users may set
it to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}; however, it is recommended to specify the problem type
for better experiment tracking and reproducibility. The allowed values
are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qp}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qcqp}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nlp}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nonconvex}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}} argument is used to assign a custom name to the model,
which is also used for naming the output directory where results
are saved. The naming behavior is as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}} is provided \(\rightarrow\) output directory uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Else if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{type}} is provided \(\rightarrow\) output directory uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{type}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Else \(\rightarrow\) output directory defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nlpoptnet}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The output directory is named using the pattern:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}model\_name\textgreater{}\_\textless{}date\textgreater{}\_\textless{}time\textgreater{}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model\_name}} is determined by the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{type}} argument

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{date}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{time}} are automatically generated timestamps

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Example\_QP\_Model\_20260423\_104512}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qp\_20260423\_104512}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nlpoptnet\_20260423\_104512}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Defining the Problem}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/defining-the-problem:defining-the-problem}}\label{\detokenize{user-guide/defining-the-problem::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This notebook provides the way of defining the model in NLPOpt\sphinxhyphen{}Net. You can define block of constraints when you have exploitable structure and also can define explicit constraitns. Along with objective and constraints this notebook provides the method of defining variable bounds that can be parameter independent or parameter dependent. We consider the general form of the problem as follows:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
\min_y &\,\, f(x,y)\\
\textrm{s.t.} &\, \, g(x,y) \leq 0 \\
&\, \, h(x,y) = 0 \\
&\, \, l(x) \leq y \leq u(x)
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The general workflow for defining a model in NLPOpt\sphinxhyphen{}Net is as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Configure training settings

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NLPOptNet}} object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define the variables and parameters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define the objective, constraints, variable bounds

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define parameter space

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Build the model

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Train and infer

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Creating the Model Object}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/defining-the-problem:creating-the-model-object}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ensure that all required configuration fields are provided. Optional parameters can be specified based on user preference. In this example we only provide the required configuration fields.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nlpoptnet}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{NLPOptNet}

\PYG{n}{CONFIG} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{epochs}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1000}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{batch\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{40}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{learning\PYGZus{}rate}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1e\PYGZhy{}3}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{hidden\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{64}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{hidden\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{n}{model} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{NLPOptNet}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{config}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{CONFIG}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{name}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Example\PYGZus{}Model}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Defining the Variables and Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/defining-the-problem:defining-the-variables-and-parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can define the parameter and variable names explicitly or by providing a list of strings.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
parameter\PYGZus{}set = model.add\PYGZus{}parameter([parameter\PYGZus{}1, parameter\PYGZus{}2, ...])
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parameter\_set}}: handle to the defined parameters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parameter\_i}}: user\sphinxhyphen{}defined string identifiers (e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"temperature"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"pressure"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"x1"}},…)

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
variable\PYGZus{}set = model.add\PYGZus{}variable([variable\PYGZus{}1, variable\PYGZus{}2, ...])
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{variable\_set}}: handle to the defined variables

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{variable\_i}}: user\sphinxhyphen{}defined string identifiers (e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"flow"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"y1"}}, …)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is convenient to define explicitely when system has few parameters and variables.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{x} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}parameter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{x1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{x2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{y} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}variable}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{y1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{y2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{y3}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{y4}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a large number of parameters and variables you may consider the following:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{no\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}parameters} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{50}
\PYG{n}{no\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}variables} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}
\PYG{n}{parameter\PYGZus{}names} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{x}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{range}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{no\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}parameters}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{n}{variable\PYGZus{}names} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{y}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{range}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{no\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}variables}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{n}{x} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}parameter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{parameter\PYGZus{}names}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{y} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}variable}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{variable\PYGZus{}names}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Extracting Model Constants from Previously Saved Files}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/defining-the-problem:extracting-model-constants-from-previously-saved-files}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently we support loading arrays from a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.npz}} file. The model will automatically resgister the contained arrays as model constants.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{extract}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{DATA\PYGZus{}DIRECTORY} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{problem.npz}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This will load all arrays stored in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{problem.npz}}. The following is an example of the output:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Loaded problem constants: {[}‘A’, ‘B’, ‘C’, ‘L’, ‘Q’, ‘U’, ‘b’, ‘c’, ‘d’, ‘l’, ‘u’{]}

\sphinxAtStartPar
User can use them by calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.A}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.B}}, …


\subsubsection{Defining Model Constants Directly}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/defining-the-problem:defining-model-constants-directly}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Model constants (arrays) can be added directly using the provided APIs. The following examples illustrate how to define matrices, vectors, and tensors:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Matrix (2D array)}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Q} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{A} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Vector (1D array)}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{c} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Tensor (multi\PYGZhy{}dimensional array)}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{T} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{tensor}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Model constants can be accessed directly as attributes (e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.Q}}). To view their values, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.Q.value}} or convert to a NumPy array using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{np.array(model.Q)}}.


\subsubsection{Defining the Objective}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/defining-the-problem:defining-the-objective}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The objective can be defined using built\sphinxhyphen{}in structured functions or explicitly using expressions. NLPOpt\sphinxhyphen{}Net provides several built\sphinxhyphen{}in functions to construct structured objectives:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Matrix operations}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)}        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Linear: A @ y}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{quad}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)}       \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Quadratic: y\PYGZca{}T Q y}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{batch\PYGZus{}lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Batched linear mapping}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{batch\PYGZus{}quad}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Batched quadratic form}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Elementwise nonlinear functions}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{sin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{expr}\PYG{p}{)}        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Sine}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{cos}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{expr}\PYG{p}{)}        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Cosine}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{exp}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{expr}\PYG{p}{)}        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Exponential}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{log}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{expr}\PYG{p}{)}        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Logarithm}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{sqrt}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{expr}\PYG{p}{)}       \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Square root}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{abs}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{expr}\PYG{p}{)}        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Absolute value}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Quadratic objective function}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{objective}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{quad}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{c}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Nonlinear bbjective function}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{objective}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{quad}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)}          \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 0.5 y\PYGZca{}T Q y}
                \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{c}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)}               \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} c\PYGZca{}T y}
                \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{p}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{exp}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} p\PYGZca{}T exp(y)}
                \PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Explicit expression}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{objective}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{exp}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{exp}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that parameters can also be included in the objective in similar way.


\subsubsection{Defining Constraints}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/defining-the-problem:defining-constraints}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Similar to the objective, constraints can be defined using structured functions or explicit expressions.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Linear constraints}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{equality}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{b} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{B}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{inequality}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{d} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{D}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Quadratic constraints}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{inequality}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{batch\PYGZus{}quad}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{batch\PYGZus{}lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{d}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{e} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{batch\PYGZus{}lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{E}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Nonlinear constraints}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{inequality}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{batch\PYGZus{}quad}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{batch\PYGZus{}lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{d}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{e} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{batch\PYGZus{}lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{E}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Explicit expression as constraints}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{equality}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{y1} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{y2} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{x1}\PYG{p}{,}
                               \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{y2} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{y3} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{x2}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{inequality}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{y1} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{y3} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}
                                 \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{y1} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{y2} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.5}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Defining Box/Bounding Constraints}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/defining-the-problem:defining-box-bounding-constraints}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Box constraints define lower and upper bounds on the decision variables. Bounds may be parameterized or some decision variable may be unbounded.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Parameterized bounds}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{var}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{,}
                          \PYG{n}{lower}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{l} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
                          \PYG{n}{upper}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{u} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{U}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Non\PYGZhy{}parameterized bounds}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{var}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lower}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{l}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{upper}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If only a lower or upper bound is available, provide only that bound. If a variable has no lower or upper bound, leave it unbounded by not specifying a bound for that variable. For vector bounds, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}np.inf}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{np.inf}} depending on how the bound data is represented. If the variables are unbounded do not call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.constraints.box.add}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Lower bound only}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{var}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lower}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{l}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Upper bound only}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{var}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{upper}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Example: y[0] has bounds, y[1] is unbounded}
\PYG{n}{l} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{array}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{inf}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{u} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{array}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}  \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{inf}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
After defining the objective, constraints, and bounds, the next step is to specify the parameter space.

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Defining Parameter Space}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/defining-parameter-space:defining-parameter-space}}\label{\detokenize{user-guide/defining-parameter-space::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The user must specify the parameter space from which training samples are drawn. NLPOpt\sphinxhyphen{}Net supports multiple ways to define this space.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{CSV\sphinxhyphen{}based dataset}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Users can explicitly provide parameter samples via a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.csv}} file.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each row corresponds to one sample of the parameter vector.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the most flexible option when sampling data is already available.

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Box\sphinxhyphen{}constrained space}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Users can define a box (hyper\sphinxhyphen{}rectangle) for the parameters.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_lower}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_upper}} can be scalars or vectors.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sampling is performed uniformly within the box.

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Simplex / Polytope space}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Users can define a simplex or general polytope region.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The space can be defined:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
using structured constraints, or

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
using matrix form: \(M x \leq 1\).

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Useful for constrained parameter spaces (e.g., probabilities, resource allocation).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Samples are generated within the feasible region.

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Using a \sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{.csv}} file}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/defining-parameter-space:using-a-csv-file}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
User needs to provide a valid path to read the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.csv}} file.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{dataset}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{parameters}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{path/to/parameters.csv}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Number of columns in the CSV must match the number of parameters defined

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Order of columns should be consistent with the parameter definition

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Box\sphinxhyphen{}Constrained Parameter Space}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/defining-parameter-space:box-constrained-parameter-space}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
User needs to provide both lower and upper bounds for all the parameters. User can provide a vector with different bounds for each parameter or a scalar as the same bound for all parameters.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lower}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{x\PYGZus{}lower}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{upper}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{x\PYGZus{}upper}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}samples} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{500}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Defining a Simplex}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/defining-parameter-space:defining-a-simplex}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A simplex is a \(d\)\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional polytope defined by linear constraints of the form:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}x \ge 0, \quad \mathbf{1}^\top x \le 1\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
More generally, a simplex can be represented as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}M x \le 1\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{simplex}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{M}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{M\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}samples}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{500}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Defining a Polytope Explicitly}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/defining-parameter-space:defining-a-polytope-explicitly}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Although the method is named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{simplex}}, it supports general convex polytopes defined by linear inequalities. For example, to define the following polytope:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}x_1 + x_2 + x_3 \le 1 \\
x_1 + 2x_2 \le 0.8 \\
0.5x_2 + x_3 \le 0.6 \\
x_1 + 0.5x_3 \ge 0.2\\
x_1 \ge 0, \quad x_2 \ge 0, \quad x_3 \ge 0\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{simplex}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{x1} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{x2} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{x3} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,}
              \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{x1} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{x2} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{x3} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{x1} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{x2} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.8}\PYG{p}{,}
              \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{x2} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{x3} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.6}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{x1} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{x3} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}samples}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{500}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The argument \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{num\_samples}} specifies the number of parameter samples to be generated from the defined polytope region. These sampled parameter points are used to construct the dataset for training and validation of the model.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The total number of generated samples is equal to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{num\_samples}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The samples are split into training and validation sets based on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{train\_frac}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each sample corresponds to one instance of the parametric optimization problem

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{num\_samples}} is not provided, a default value (typically \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1000}}) is used.


\subsubsection{Note}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/defining-parameter-space:note}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only one parameter space definition is required.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If multiple are provided, the most recent call will overwrite the previous definition.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of samples can be controlled via the configuration (e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{num\_samples}}).

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The user must define a parameter space for which the optimization problem is feasible.
Currently, NLPOpt\sphinxhyphen{}Net does not automatically detect infeasibility for parameter realizations.
Providing infeasible samples may lead to invalid training behavior or poor model performance.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Training and Inference}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/training-and-inference:training-and-inference}}\label{\detokenize{user-guide/training-and-inference::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
After defining the problem and configuration, the model can be built, trained, and used for inference as shown below.


\subsubsection{Build and Train}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/training-and-inference:build-and-train}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.build()}} constructs the symbolic model, prepares the dataset, and initializes the training pipeline.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model.optimize()}} trains the model and saves all artifacts, including model weights, history, summary, and metadata, to a timestamped directory.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{run\_dir}} points to the directory where results are stored.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{build}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{optimize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{run\PYGZus{}dir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Path}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{output\PYGZus{}dir}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{run\PYGZus{}dir =}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{run\PYGZus{}dir}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Model Summary and Training History Visualization}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/training-and-inference:model-summary-and-training-history-visualization}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summary()}} function prints a summary after the model is trained. It includes the model name, the size of the model, number of samples considered during training, training time, maximum constraint violation and an estimation of inference times.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{summary}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Inference time estimations are based on microbenchmarking on the training hardware and may vary across different hardware and runtime conditions.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot\_history()}} function generates a plot showing the training behavior of the model. The plot includes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Objective evolution for training and validation samples.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Constraint violation over epochs, typically shown on a logarithmic scale.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{plot\PYGZus{}history}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics[width=1.000\linewidth]{{example_history}.png}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
After training, NLPOpt\sphinxhyphen{}Net automatically saves all relevant files inside the output directory:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}model\_name\textgreater{}\_\textless{}YYYYMMDD\textgreater{}\_\textless{}HHMMSS\textgreater{}/}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following files are generated:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{metadata.json}} — Stores the complete model configuration, problem definition, architecture details, and references to all saved files. This file is used to reload the trained model.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summary.json}} — Contains aggregated training statistics such as final loss, objective values, constraint violations, dataset sizes, training time, and estimated inference times.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{history.csv}} — Stores per\sphinxhyphen{}epoch training history including training/validation loss, objective values, and constraint violations. This file is used for visualization via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot\_history()}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parameters.csv}} — Contains sampled parameter inputs \(x\) used for training and validation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{predicted\_variables.csv}} — Contains the corresponding predicted decision variables \(y\) from the trained model.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model\_weights.npz}} — Stores the full trained model weights, including both backbone and projection\sphinxhyphen{}related parameters.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{backbone\_weights.npz}} — Stores only the neural network (backbone) weights.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{problem.npz}} — Encodes the optimization problem structure (e.g., matrices, coefficients).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{problem\_constants.npz}} — Stores constant components of the problem for efficient reuse during inference.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{projection\_native.json}} — Contains metadata describing the compiled native projection backend, including platform\sphinxhyphen{}specific shared libraries stored inside the saved run folder.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Reloading the Model}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/training-and-inference:reloading-the-model}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
After training, the model can be reloaded from the saved \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{metadata.json}} file.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nlpoptnet}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{NLPOptNet}
\PYG{n}{reloaded} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{NLPOptNet}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{path/to/metadata.json}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load(...)}} function restores the trained model, including the configuration, learned weights, problem definition, and available inference backends from the saved run directory. A parameter sample can then be provided to the trained model to compute the corresponding prediction. NLPOpt\sphinxhyphen{}Net supports two projection backends during inference.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}pred\PYGZus{}native} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{reloaded}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{predict}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{projection\PYGZus{}backend}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{native}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}pred\PYGZus{}jax} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{reloaded}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{predict}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{projection\PYGZus{}backend}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{jax}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{jax}} — Uses the JAX\sphinxhyphen{}based implementation of the projection layer. This backend is fully portable and supports efficient batch inference.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{native}} — Uses a compiled native (C\sphinxhyphen{}based) implementation of the projection layer. This backend is optimized for fast single\sphinxhyphen{}sample inference and is recommended for deployment.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{native}} backend, a C compiler must be installed on the system. The saved run keeps native binaries under its own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{native\_projection/}} folder, and if a model is reloaded on a different supported OS/architecture, NLPOpt\sphinxhyphen{}Net will compile a matching native binary for the current system into that same run directory.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{examples/index:examples}}\label{\detokenize{examples/index::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This section provides synthetic examples showing how to formulate and solve
quadratic programs, quadratically constrained quadratic programs, and nonlinear
programs using the package.

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Quadratic Programs (QPs)}
\label{\detokenize{examples/01_Example_QP:quadratic-programs-qps}}\label{\detokenize{examples/01_Example_QP::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider the following QP problem:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
\min_{y} \quad & \frac{1}{2} y^\top Q y + c^\top y \\
\text{s.t.} \quad
& A y = b + B x, \\
& C y \leq d, \\
& l + L x \leq y \leq u + U x,
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where, \(Q\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\succeq0\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n_\textrm{eq}\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{n_\textrm{eq}}\), \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n_\textrm{eq}\times p}\), \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{n_\textrm{ineq}\times n}\), \(d\in\mathbb{R}^{n_\textrm{ineq}}\), \(l\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(L\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(U\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\). The goal is to find optimal \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) for different parameter realizations \(x\in\mathbb{R}^p\). For this example consider, \(n=10, p=5,n_\textrm{eq}=5,n_\textrm{ineq}=5\).


\subsubsection{Import Libraries}
\label{\detokenize{examples/01_Example_QP:import-libraries}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{numpy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{np}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pandas}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pd}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nlpoptnet}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{NLPOptNet}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsection{Quadratically Constrained Quadratic Programs (QCQPs)}
\label{\detokenize{examples/02_Example_QCQP:quadratically-constrained-quadratic-programs-qcqps}}\label{\detokenize{examples/02_Example_QCQP::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider the following QCQP problem:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
\min_{y} \quad & \frac{1}{2} y^\top Q y + c^\top y \\
\text{s.t.} \quad
& A y = b + B x, \\
& y^\top C_i y + d_i^\top y \leq \beta_i + E_i x, \quad i = 1, 2, \ldots, m_i, \\
& l + L x \leq y \leq u + U x.
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where, \(Q \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n} \succeq 0\), \(c \in \mathbb{R}^n\), \(A \in \mathbb{R}^{n_{\mathrm{eq}} \times n}\), \(b \in \mathbb{R}^{n_{\mathrm{eq}}}\), \(B \in \mathbb{R}^{n_{\mathrm{eq}} \times p }\), \(C_i \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n} \succeq 0\), \(d_i \in \mathbb{R}^n\), \(\beta_i \in \mathbb{R}\), \(E_i \in \mathbb{R}^{1 \times p}\) for \(i = 1, 2, \ldots, n_{\mathrm{ineq}}\), \(l \in \mathbb{R}^n\), \(L \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times p}\), \(u \in \mathbb{R}^n\), and \(U \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times p}\). We must learn to approximate the optimal solution \(y \in \mathbb{R}^n\) given a parameter realization \(x \in \mathbb{R}^p\). For this example consider, \(n=10, p=5,n_\textrm{eq}=5,n_\textrm{ineq}=5\).

\subsection{NonLinear Programs (NLPs)}
\label{\detokenize{examples/03_Example_NLP:nonlinear-programs-nlps}}\label{\detokenize{examples/03_Example_NLP::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider the following QCQP problem:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
\min_{y} \quad & \frac{1}{2} y^\top Q y + c^\top y \\
\text{s.t.} \quad
& A y = b + B x, \\
& a_i^\top \exp(y) + y^\top W y \leq \beta_i + E_i x, \quad i = 1, 2, \ldots, m_i, \\
& l + L x \leq y \leq u + U x.
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where, \(Q \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n} \succeq 0\), \(c \in \mathbb{R}^n\), \(A \in \mathbb{R}^{n_{\textrm{eq}} \times n}\), \(b \in \mathbb{R}^{n_{\textrm{eq}}}\), \(B \in \mathbb{R}^{n_{\textrm{eq}} \times p}\), \(a_i \in \mathbb{R}^n\), \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n} \succeq 0\), \(\beta_i \in \mathbb{R}\), \(E_i \in \mathbb{R}^{1 \times p}\) for \(i = 1,2,\ldots,n_{\textrm{ineq}}\), \(l \in \mathbb{R}^n\), \(L \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times p}\), \(u \in \mathbb{R}^n\), and \(U \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times p}\). The parameter \(x \in \mathbb{R}^p\) varies across problem instances. We aim to learn to approximate the optimal solution \(y \in \mathbb{R}^n\) given a parameter realization \(x\). For this example consider, \(n=10, p=5,n_\textrm{eq}=5,n_\textrm{ineq}=5\).

\label{\detokenize{api/package/object:role-of-the-object}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NLPOptNet}} is responsible for:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
storing symbolic parameters and variables,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tracking constants and extracted problem data,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
recording objectives and constraints,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
loading or sampling parameter data,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
building the trainable model,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
training, saving, loading, and predicting.

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{Notes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NLPOptNet}} is designed around parametric optimization problems of the
form
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
    \min_y \quad & f(y, x) \\
    \text{s.t.}\quad & h(y, x) = 0, \\
    & g(y, x) \le 0, \\
    & \ell(x) \le y \le u(x),
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(x\) is the parameter vector and \(y\) is the decision
vector. The learned model approximates the mapping
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}x \mapsto y^\star(x)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
by combining:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a symbolic problem definition,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a neural backbone that predicts warm starts,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a projection layer that enforces local feasibility structure.

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{Notes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The projection\sphinxhyphen{}oriented part of the training loop can be viewed as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}(\hat y, \hat \lambda, \hat \mu) = \Phi_\theta(x), \qquad
(y^\star, \lambda^\star, \mu^\star) = \Pi(\hat y, \hat \lambda, \hat \mu; x),\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k\_layer}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cp\_mode}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cp\_iters}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cp\_tol}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{safety}}, and
the Ruiz\sphinxhyphen{}scaling options control the projection operator \(\Pi\).

\end{fulllineitems}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{objective}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{quad}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{c}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{sin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Callable objectives}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/objective:callable-objectives}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{objective}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{params}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{vars}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{y\PYGZus{}value} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{vars}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{y}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{y\PYGZus{}value} \PYG{o}{@} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Q} \PYG{o}{@} \PYG{n}{y\PYGZus{}value} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{c} \PYG{o}{@} \PYG{n}{y\PYGZus{}value}

\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{objective}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{objective}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Important note}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/objective:important-note}}

Callable objectives are flexible, but runs built from raw Python callables are not automatically reconstructible from saved metadata alone.

    \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{y2} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{y3} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{x2} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Structured affine:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{equality}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{b} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{B}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{equality\PYGZus{}block}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{params}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{vars}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{x\PYGZus{}value} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{params}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{x}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{equality}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{equality\PYGZus{}block}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{C}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{d} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{D}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}

\subsubsection{Box}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/constraints/box:box}}\label{\detokenize{api/package/constraints/box::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Box constraints are kept on a dedicated path instead of being merged into the general inequality residuals.


\paragraph{Affine vector bounds}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/constraints/box:affine-vector-bounds}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{var}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{lower}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{l} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{upper}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{u} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{lin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{U}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Scalar bounds}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/constraints/box:scalar-bounds}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraints}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{box}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{y1} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{y2} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Why this matters}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/constraints/box:why-this-matters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The internal implementation converts box bounds into affine lower and upper bound operators, which are then enforced directly inside the projection layer.

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Execution}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/index:execution}}\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/index::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Execution is split into four steps.

\sphinxstepscope


\subsubsection{Building}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/building:building}}\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/building::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The build stage is triggered with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/package/object:nlpoptnet.api.NLPOptNet.build}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nlpoptnet.api.NLPOptNet.build()}}}}}.


\paragraph{What build does}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/building:what-build-does}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
validates the model definition,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
normalizes the configuration,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
constructs the symbolic \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{jaxmodel}} problem,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
prepares bound operators,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
loads or samples parameter data,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
splits train and validation data,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
prepares fixed batches,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
initializes the trainable backbone and projection pipeline,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
optionally runs a JIT warmup pass.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Typical use}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/building:typical-use}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{dataset}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{parameters}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{notebooks/data/qp/parameters.csv}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{build}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxstepscope


\subsubsection{Training}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/training:training}}\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/training::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The training stage is triggered with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/package/object:nlpoptnet.api.NLPOptNet.optimize}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nlpoptnet.api.NLPOptNet.optimize()}}}}}.


\paragraph{Returned value}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/training:returned-value}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{optimize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{output\PYGZus{}dir}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{metadata\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The returned dictionary contains:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{output\_dir}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{metadata\_path}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summary}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{history}}

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Saved artifacts}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/training:saved-artifacts}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Training writes a timestamped run directory containing:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{metadata.json}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summary.json}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{history.csv}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parameters.csv}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{predicted\_variables.csv}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{model\_weights.npz}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{backbone\_weights.npz}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{problem\_constants.npz}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{problem.npz}} when the problem was extracted from disk

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{projection\_native.json}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\subsubsection{Loading}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/loading:loading}}\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/loading::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Saved runs can be restored with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/package/object:nlpoptnet.api.NLPOptNet.load}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nlpoptnet.api.NLPOptNet.load()}}}}}.


\paragraph{Example}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/loading:example}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{restored} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{NLPOptNet}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{restored}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{demo\PYGZus{}qp\PYGZus{}20260416\PYGZus{}120000/metadata.json}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Limitations}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/loading:limitations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatic reload is supported for serializable symbolic problems. Runs that depend on raw Python objective callables or callable constraint blocks are intentionally rejected during \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load(...)}} because the original Python code is not reconstructed from metadata.

\sphinxstepscope


\subsubsection{Predicting}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/predicting:predicting}}\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/predicting::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Predictions are produced with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/package/object:nlpoptnet.api.NLPOptNet.predict}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nlpoptnet.api.NLPOptNet.predict()}}}}}.


\paragraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/predicting:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Single sample:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{prediction} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{predict}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Batch:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{batch\PYGZus{}prediction} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{predict}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.5}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Backend selection:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{predict}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{projection\PYGZus{}backend}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{auto}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{predict}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{projection\PYGZus{}backend}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{jax}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{model}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{predict}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{projection\PYGZus{}backend}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{native}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Runtime summary}
\label{\detokenize{api/package/execution/predicting:runtime-summary}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The compact run summary is available through {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/package/object:nlpoptnet.api.NLPOptNet.summary}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nlpoptnet.api.NLPOptNet.summary()}}}}}, and history plots can be created with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/package/object:nlpoptnet.api.NLPOptNet.plot_history}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nlpoptnet.api.NLPOptNet.plot\_history()}}}}}.

\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{class\DUrole{w}{ }}}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{jaxmodel.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{HighLevelNLPBuilder}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{dtype=\textless{}class \textquotesingle{}jax.numpy.float64\textquotesingle{}\textgreater{}}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{object}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
High\sphinxhyphen{}level modeling interface for parametric nonlinear programs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This builder assembles problems of the form
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
    \min_y \quad & f(y, x) \\
    \text{s.t.}\quad & h(y, x) = 0, \\
    & g(y, x) \le 0, \\
    & \ell(x) \le y \le u(x),
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(x\) denotes the parameter vector and \(y\) denotes the
decision variables.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It provides a more convenient interface than the lower\sphinxhyphen{}level
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/core/jaxmodel/builder:jaxmodel.builder.NLPBuilder}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{jaxmodel.builder.NLPBuilder}}}}} for assembling:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
parameter blocks,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
variable blocks,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
objectives,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
affine, quadratic, and nonlinear constraints,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
affine lower and upper bounds.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{class\DUrole{w}{ }}}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{jaxmodel.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{QuadraticObjective}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{Q}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Array}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{c}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Array}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{constant}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{0.0}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{object}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Represent a quadratic objective in the flat variable vector.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The objective is modeled as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}f(y) = \frac{1}{2} y^\top Q y + c^\top y + k\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(y \in \mathbf{R}^n\) is the packed decision\sphinxhyphen{}variable vector,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(Q \in \mathbf{R}^{n \times n}\) is the quadratic matrix,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(c \in \mathbf{R}^n\) is the linear coefficient vector,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(k \in \mathbf{R}\) is a constant offset.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This structured form is useful because the gradient and Hessian are known
analytically:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\nabla f(y) = Q y + c,\qquad \nabla^2 f(y) = Q\end{split}
\end{equation*}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{object}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Container for one residual block in the optimization model.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each constraint entry represents either an equality residual
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}h(y, x) = 0\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
or an inequality residual
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}g(y, x) \le 0\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
written in residual form with respect to the packed variable vector
\(y\) and parameter vector \(x\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fun}} callable returns the residual block, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{jac\_y\_fun}} stores
an optional Jacobian with respect to \(y\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{object}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Differentiable nonlinear program in packed\sphinxhyphen{}vector form.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{JaxNLPModel}} represents a parametric optimization problem as a set of
JAX\sphinxhyphen{}callable evaluators over a flat decision\sphinxhyphen{}variable vector \(y\) and
parameter dictionary \(x\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The model is organized around the canonical form
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
    \min_y \quad & f(y, x) \\
    \text{s.t.}\quad & h(y, x) = 0, \\
    & g(y, x) \le 0, \\
    & \ell(x) \le y \le u(x).
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to evaluating the objective and residuals, the model exposes
derivatives and local approximations used by the projection and training
pipeline:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\nabla_y f,\qquad \nabla_y^2 f,\qquad
\nabla_y h,\qquad \nabla_y g\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and SQP\sphinxhyphen{}style local subproblem data.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialize the model and optionally JIT\sphinxhyphen{}compile its evaluators.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{object}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Container for one residual block in the optimization model.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each constraint entry represents either an equality residual
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}h(y, x) = 0\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
or an inequality residual
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}g(y, x) \le 0\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
written in residual form with respect to the packed variable vector
\(y\) and parameter vector \(x\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fun}} callable returns the residual block, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{jac\_y\_fun}} stores
an optional Jacobian with respect to \(y\).

\subsubsection{jaxmodel.highlevel}
\label{\detokenize{api/core/jaxmodel/highlevel:module-jaxmodel.highlevel}}\label{\detokenize{api/core/jaxmodel/highlevel:jaxmodel-highlevel}}\label{\detokenize{api/core/jaxmodel/highlevel::doc}}\index{module@\spxentry{module}!jaxmodel.highlevel@\spxentry{jaxmodel.highlevel}}\index{jaxmodel.highlevel@\spxentry{jaxmodel.highlevel}!module@\spxentry{module}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
High\sphinxhyphen{}level symbolic builder for structured parametric optimization models.
\index{HighLevelNLPBuilder (class in jaxmodel.highlevel)@\spxentry{HighLevelNLPBuilder}\spxextra{class in jaxmodel.highlevel}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api/core/jaxmodel/highlevel:jaxmodel.highlevel.HighLevelNLPBuilder}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{class\DUrole{w}{ }}}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{jaxmodel.highlevel.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{HighLevelNLPBuilder}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{dtype=\textless{}class \textquotesingle{}jax.numpy.float64\textquotesingle{}\textgreater{}}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{object}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
High\sphinxhyphen{}level modeling interface for parametric nonlinear programs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This builder assembles problems of the form
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
    \min_y \quad & f(y, x) \\
    \text{s.t.}\quad & h(y, x) = 0, \\
    & g(y, x) \le 0, \\
    & \ell(x) \le y \le u(x),
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(x\) denotes the parameter vector and \(y\) denotes the
decision variables.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It provides a more convenient interface than the lower\sphinxhyphen{}level
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/core/jaxmodel/builder:jaxmodel.builder.NLPBuilder}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{jaxmodel.builder.NLPBuilder}}}}} for assembling:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
parameter blocks,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
variable blocks,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
objectives,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
affine, quadratic, and nonlinear constraints,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
affine lower and upper bounds.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialize an empty high\sphinxhyphen{}level model builder.

\subsubsection{jaxmodel.model}
\label{\detokenize{api/core/jaxmodel/model:module-jaxmodel.model}}\label{\detokenize{api/core/jaxmodel/model:jaxmodel-model}}\label{\detokenize{api/core/jaxmodel/model::doc}}\index{module@\spxentry{module}!jaxmodel.model@\spxentry{jaxmodel.model}}\index{jaxmodel.model@\spxentry{jaxmodel.model}!module@\spxentry{module}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api/core/jaxmodel/model:jaxmodel.model.JaxNLPModel}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{class\DUrole{w}{ }}}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{jaxmodel.model.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{JaxNLPModel}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{var\_spec: \textasciitilde{}jaxmodel.variables.VariableSpec}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{objective\_fun}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{constraints: \textasciitilde{}typing.Sequence{[}\textasciitilde{}jaxmodel.constraints.ConstraintEntry{]} | None = None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{bounds: \textasciitilde{}jaxmodel.bounds.BoundSpec | None = None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{parameter\_spec: \textasciitilde{}jaxmodel.parameters.ParameterSpec | None = None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{dtype=\textless{}class \textquotesingle{}jax.numpy.float64\textquotesingle{}\textgreater{}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{jit\_compile: bool = True}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{object}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Differentiable nonlinear program in packed\sphinxhyphen{}vector form.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{JaxNLPModel}} represents a parametric optimization problem as a set of
JAX\sphinxhyphen{}callable evaluators over a flat decision\sphinxhyphen{}variable vector \(y\) and
parameter dictionary \(x\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The model is organized around the canonical form
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
    \min_y \quad & f(y, x) \\
    \text{s.t.}\quad & h(y, x) = 0, \\
    & g(y, x) \le 0, \\
    & \ell(x) \le y \le u(x).
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to evaluating the objective and residuals, the model exposes
derivatives and local approximations used by the projection and training
pipeline:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\nabla_y f,\qquad \nabla_y^2 f,\qquad
\nabla_y h,\qquad \nabla_y g\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and SQP\sphinxhyphen{}style local subproblem data.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialize the model and optionally JIT\sphinxhyphen{}compile its evaluators.

\index{QuadraticObjective (class in jaxmodel.objective)@\spxentry{QuadraticObjective}\spxextra{class in jaxmodel.objective}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api/core/jaxmodel/objective:jaxmodel.objective.QuadraticObjective}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{class\DUrole{w}{ }}}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{jaxmodel.objective.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{QuadraticObjective}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{Q}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Array}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{c}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Array}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{constant}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{0.0}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{object}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Represent a quadratic objective in the flat variable vector.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The objective is modeled as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}f(y) = \frac{1}{2} y^\top Q y + c^\top y + k\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(y \in \mathbf{R}^n\) is the packed decision\sphinxhyphen{}variable vector,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(Q \in \mathbf{R}^{n \times n}\) is the quadratic matrix,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(c \in \mathbf{R}^n\) is the linear coefficient vector,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(k \in \mathbf{R}\) is a constant offset.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This structured form is useful because the gradient and Hessian are known
analytically:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\nabla f(y) = Q y + c,\qquad \nabla^2 f(y) = Q\end{split}
\end{equation*}\index{Q (jaxmodel.objective.QuadraticObjective attribute)@\spxentry{Q}\spxextra{jaxmodel.objective.QuadraticObjective attribute}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Module}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
MLP backbone that predicts primal and dual warm starts.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a parameter vector \(x\), the backbone predicts
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}(\hat y, \hat \lambda, \hat \mu) = \Phi_\theta(x)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\hat y\) is the warm start for the primal variables,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\hat \lambda\) is the warm start for equality multipliers,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\hat \mu\) is the warm start for inequality multipliers.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These predictions are then corrected by the projection layer so the final
output better respects the optimization problem structure.
